data.hypothesis: Split source ranges with rsqrtf and factor-four unrolling produced the best recorded mean (0.00089948 s), while the corresponding factor-eight candidate measured 0.00101347 s. Testing factor-two unrolling holds the split-range and arithmetic choices fixed while probing whether less unrolling reduces code or register overhead without giving up useful loop-control savings. These search measurements do not establish causality or predict this candidate's result.

memory_lessons.applicability: These are search measurements for this campaign; use them to motivate a controlled comparison, not to claim a general speedup.
memory_lessons.claim: The split-range control-only candidate measured 0.00184358 s versus the 0.00184441 s baseline, while split ranges with rsqrtf and factor-four unrolling measured 0.00089948 s. The factor-eight variant of that combination measured 0.00101347 s. The combination is promising, but the measurements do not isolate the cause of the difference.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Validate and compare the factor-two variant against the factor-four and factor-eight candidates under the official protocol, including coincident positions and extreme mass.

data.notes: Only the CUDA kernel is changed. The launch configuration, one-target-per-thread mapping, target-mass arithmetic, and ascending interaction order are retained. The controller must validate all correctness cases and measure all scored sizes; no result is presumed.
transformations: Replace the conditional all-source loop with ascending ranges [0, i) and (i, n), so the self-interaction is never evaluated.
Use rsqrtf(distSq) and multiply by its cube in each interaction, retaining target-mass multiplication and final per-target-mass division.
Apply #pragma unroll 2 to both split source loops to test a lower unroll factor than the previously measured factor-four and factor-eight variants.
Preserve one target per thread, the existing integration arithmetic, and the launch configuration; add no shared-memory tiling or multi-target coarsening.
